Bar holds: a full attack round found no failing trace, and `npm test` is green (56/56). Taking `e-red-team-pass` → `done`.

## Run summary — outcome: success

**Dispatches:** 2 of 12 (builder ×1, red-team ×1); rounds of the `attack` loop: 0 (no `e-red-team-fail` traversal was needed).

**Builder (round 0)** rewrote `parseCsvLine` in `src/csv.mjs` as a single-pass index-based scanner (removed the O(n²) `rest.slice(1)` loop). It strips exactly one trailing `\n`/`\r\n` before parsing, so `"a\n` is an unterminated-quote `CsvError` while `"a\n"` → `["a\n"]`; any `"` outside quotes, anything but `,`/end after a closing quote, and any other unquoted `\r`/`\n` are `CsvError`; every other code unit is literal. `tests/csv.test.mjs` grew from 4 to 56 tests, including perf tests on 100 KB–1 MB pathological inputs, an exhaustive sweep of all strings up to length 6 over `{" , \n \r a}` against an independent reference parser, and random fuzzing asserting only `string[]` or `CsvError` ever comes out. `CHANGES.md` records this.

**Red team (round 1)** attacked with source review of the index boundaries, an exhaustive differential over all 488,281 strings of length 0–8, ~800k random differential cases with Unicode oddities, targeted terminator/escape edge cases, 15+ non-string input shapes, and 24 pathological shapes at 100 KB/1 MB/10 MB (worst 2.9 ms at 100 KB). It found no reproducible failure; `ATTACK.md` documents the attack. Verdict: **pass**. Noted as out of contract scope and not exercised: builtin-prototype tampering and strings near V8's max length.

Working tree is uncommitted (no commit was requested). Files changed/added: `src/csv.mjs`, `tests/csv.test.mjs`, `CHANGES.md`, `ATTACK.md`.
